chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: Studying orchestration with Hale Smith for a youth symphony piece
summary: Budd takes on a Kennedy Center commission and learns orchestration from Hale Smith and Piston's book.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So I'm in the process of doing that now, and actually it's a new experience for me in writing because I knew it was a big assignment but just like I said I can't say no and I think that well I'd better go to the horse's mouth and find out what to do so I'm in the process now of studying with Hale Smith who's assistant director of music at the University of Connecticut. And he's actually a great symphony writer. So I told Hale, I said, Hale, I took on this assignment and I really don't know nothing about symphonies. He says --
You've been saying that all your life, haven't you.
He says, you can do it man, you can do it. I says, well man, well what should I do? I mean, you
know, tell me, you know. He says well look, you just write, he says you write. He says now here. So we would sit down, he would show me different colorings, you know.

Yeah, he would say now, you know, with your clarinets and your oboes he says, you don't want to write one, two, three, four, one, two, three,four. He says you sandwich them in, you know, for color, in your flutes and things, and you tie them in.

He showed me the technicalities. And with all of these different transposing instruments incidents, I'm having trouble with them. I don't have too much trouble with the strings but he said here, I want you to take this book and he says you just write. So he gave me a great book on orchestration by Piston, which has opened my eyes to all of these different textures and what not. So I'm going for myself, I'm writing it to him, in fact sometimes -- tomorrow I'm going over -- I've written 25 pages of music, I'm going to go on before I keep going too far --
Let him CHECK it Before you chicken out.
--and let him check it out. He says you go ahead and write and I won't let you go wrong.
